react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the eight differentially abundant metabolites identified two dominant biological themes. The first and most compelling is eicosanoid and arachidonic-acid metabolism. The WikiPathways pathway 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WP:WP167) achieved rank 1 in the RaMP multi-database ORA with an FDR of 6.18e-14 and a raw p-value of 4.41e-16, with five of the eight input metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717) — hitting the 27-member pathway, yielding a fold enrichment of 1429.7. This same biological domain was independently confirmed by mummichog's m/z-direct analysis, where 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' ranked first (p=0.00109) with eleven input metabolites overlapping, including all five of the above plus the prostaglandin B1 surrogate. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) as the top-ranked hit with the same four metabolites. The second biological theme centers on sulfur amino-acid metabolism. MetaboAnalystR detected KEGG:hsa00670 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism) at rank 1 among the non-lipid pathways (p=0.0051), driven by L-cysteine (C00097) and L-cystathionine (C02291). Mummichog independently reported 'Methionine and cysteine metabolism' (p=0.050), confirming the same two compounds. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all eight input compounds are structurally distinct with no alias conflicts. Notably, mercaptopurine (C02380) is absent from both enriched pathway clusters, suggesting it is either a standalone perturbation or reflects a treatment-specific pharmacodynamic effect not captured by the curated pathway libraries used.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites were analysed across three complementary enrichment paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked hit with FDR 6.18e-14 and raw p-value 4.41e-16; five metabolites overlapped its 27-member roster (leukotriene A4, arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE). The same five metabolites appeared in seven NSAID drug-action pathways from SMPDB (FDR 3.04e-13), reflecting their shared arachidonate substrate. Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis independently confirmed Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top pathway (p-value 0.00160), overlapping 11 compounds including the five RaMP hits plus prostaglandin B1 and leukotriene B4. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA corroborated KEGG:hsa00670 at rank 1 among non-lipid pathways (p-value 0.0051) with L-cystathionine and L-cysteine as the two overlapping metabolites; KEGG:hsa00270 ranked 3 (p-value 0.0082). Mercaptopurine did not map to either enriched cluster, suggesting it represents a pharmacodynamic outlier not captured by the curated libraries used.
